A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DCCD-CONF research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial experimental additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic causal-discovery experiments and Perturb-CITE-seq predictive results, with additional empirical analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds synthetic sensitivity studies, runtime comparisons, gene-expression evaluations, and protein-signaling graph-recovery results.

M1.justification: The implicit-flow causal model, Gaussian confounder representation, likelihood objective, alternating optimization, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The noncontractive preconditioning adaptation already appears in v1. Revised regularization values concern experimental settings rather than a new method.

E1.justification: Appendix C.8 adds the Sachs protein-signaling benchmark, extending real-data evaluation from gene-expression prediction without a known causal graph to structure recovery against a consensus biological network. Perturb-CITE-seq and synthetic SEM evaluations remain; the synthetic studies additionally sample intermediate degrees of nonlinearity and controlled cycle counts.

E2.justification: The main synthetic comparisons replace DCDI with DAGMA and ADMG, and the intervention-count comparison expands beyond LLC. Appendix C adds LiNGAM-MMI comparisons; the new gene-expression MAE table evaluates Bicycle and DCDFG, while the Sachs table evaluates DAG-GNN, DAGMA, and NOTEARS. DCDI remains in the unchanged NLL table and earlier appendix comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported synthetic samples per intervention decrease from 1000 to 500. Appendix B.3 changes lambda from 0.001 to 0.01 and rho from 0.01 to 0.1. v2 also introduces JCI-based evaluation of DAGMA/ADMG and gene-expression I-MAE evaluation. The node-scaling confounder ratio changes to 0.3 in Section 4.1 but remains 0.4 in Appendix B.4.1, leaving that setting inconsistent. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled cycle-count and nonlinearity sweeps, a regularization sensitivity grid, a runtime comparison, and analysis of the recovered Co-Culture graph. These examine structural difficulty, parameter dependence, computational cost, and biological feedback. The earlier noncontractive, sample-size, noise, and edge-density analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 already reports trial standard deviations in Table 1 and displays uncertainty bands. The new checklist explicitly identifies plot and table uncertainty as standard deviations over repeated trials, extending the reporting explanation. Neither version supplies run counts or seeds; the added MAE table follows the existing mean-and-standard-deviation convention.

E6.justification: v2 revises and expands the main synthetic results and removes the separate linear confounder-count and node-scaling result panels. New Table 3 reports Co-Culture MAE of 0.765 for DCCD-CONF versus 0.735 for Bicycle. New Table 4 reports Sachs SHD of 18 versus 19, 21, and 22 for DAG-GNN, DAGMA, and NOTEARS. Runtime, sensitivity, and 38 inferred feedback cycles are also newly reported. Table 1 and Figures 6-8 retain their results; changed settings prevent interpreting revised synthetic scores as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 revises the meta-system equation to condition intervention replacement on an active context. Appendix A.3 adds the reverse direction of differing sigma-separation statements to the proof of Theorem 2, although the subsequent argument does not separately resolve that added case. The theorem statement, formal assumptions, and most derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: differentiable nonlinear cyclic discovery with Gaussian confounding, identification of an interventional equivalence class through score maximization, and empirical advantages over existing methods. Added experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies comparative performance in near-linear and few-intervention settings, explains LLC's runtime advantage through its regression-based procedure, and interprets recovered gene-network cycles as evidence of biological feedback. It also adds a hyperparameter-robustness interpretation. The stated Gaussian-noise limitation and future directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Sections 4 and B.3 replace a promised public release with a stated repository location, add implementation sources for DAGMA/ADMG and LiNGAM-MMI, and revise regularization values. Appendix C.6 specifies 200 epochs for the runtime experiment. Existing architecture, optimizer, hardware, thresholds, and gene-data preprocessing disclosures largely remain unchanged; repository availability is only reported by the PDF.

R1.justification: The introduction adds discussion and citations concerning LiNGAM/MMI, integer-programming approaches, and doubly robust causal inference; DAGMA and Bicycle also enter the references. These broaden the literature coverage while retaining the original positioning around jointly handling nonlinearity, cycles, confounding, and interventions.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section structure are retained. Changes comprise localized related-work and experimental rewrites, short methodological explanations, wording corrections, acknowledgments, and a new checklist. Appendix C gains subsections without a wholesale reorganization of the existing argument.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially rebuilt around confounders, cycles, nonlinearity, and interventions, while node scaling moves into Figure 3 with a revised comparator display. v2 adds Figures 9-13 and Tables 3-4, including sensitivity heatmaps, runtime bars, and recovered-network matrices. Existing appendix figures and tables are also relocated and the NLL table is reformatted.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides useful tests of the central cycle/nonlinearity claims, broader comparisons, runtime evidence, and real biological structure-recovery evaluation. These improve empirical scrutiny. However, conflicting node-scaling settings and the mismatch between Appendix C.5's hyperparameter ranges and Figure 10 limit reproducibility; the figure also does not support the stated robustness for most combinations. The net improvement is therefore limited despite the substantial expansion.
